rubric:
1. Structures the pipeline: query understanding (spelling, category and attribute extraction, synonyms), retrieval that combines lexical matching (BM25 or an inverted index) with semantic retrieval (embeddings and ANN), then a learning-to-rank model over the top few hundred, then business rules and diversity.
2. Defines labels from logs with graded relevance (for example purchase > add to cart > click > skip) and addresses position bias (randomisation, click models, or inverse propensity weighting); mentions human relevance judgments for evaluation sets.
3. Describes ranking features and model: query-product text match, embedding similarity, price, ratings, popularity, availability, personalisation, with a pointwise, pairwise or listwise objective (for example LambdaMART or a neural ranker).
4. Evaluates offline with ranking metrics (nDCG, MRR, recall at k) on held-out queries, including head versus tail queries and null-result rate, and online with an A/B test on conversion or revenue per search with latency and zero-result guardrails.
5. Discusses trade-offs and edge cases: tail queries with no history, new products (cold start), relevance versus revenue, and latency budget per stage.
